title: Spain's civil war became the world's war.

post.caption: Spain 1936–1939, Part 2: Madrid, the International Brigades, Guernica, the Ebro — and the end of the Civil War. Images: public domain.

ebro.credit: Republican soldiers decorated after the Ebro offensive (photograph, Aug 1938)

beats.text: Spain's civil war became the world's war.
November 1936. Franco's army reached Madrid. The city held. Its slogan went around the world: they shall not pass.
beats.say: November nineteen thirty-six. Franco's army reached Madrid. The city held. Its slogan went around the world: they shall not pass.

beats.text: Volunteers from dozens of countries came to fight for the Republic: the International Brigades.
Hitler and Mussolini sent Franco planes, tanks and troops. Stalin sent the Republic weapons.
On a busy Monday, German and Italian bombers destroyed the Basque town of Guernica. Picasso painted it, and the world saw it.
Behind both front lines, tens of thousands of civilians were killed for who they were, or what they believed.
In 1938, the Republic gambled on one last offensive at the Ebro. It lasted four months, and failed.
beats.say: In nineteen thirty-eight, the Republic gambled on one last offensive at the Ebro. It lasted four months, and failed.

beats.text: Catalonia fell. Hundreds of thousands fled across the snow into France, and ended up in camps on the beach.
On the first of April 1939, Franco announced: the war is over. He would rule Spain for thirty-six years.
beats.say: On the first of April nineteen thirty-nine, Franco announced: the war is over. He would rule Spain for thirty-six years.
